prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the molecular basis of thalidomide-class molecular glues

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation turns a biological process, ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis, into a defined chemical reaction that can be programmed: a bifunctional molecule or a glue forms a ternary complex and the target is removed instead of inhibited. It gave biologists a general tool as well as a new drug modality, and the cereblon work gave a mechanistic explanation for thalidomide-class drugs that had been used for decades without one. Reproduction is broad across many laboratories and target classes. I keep Handa in the trio because the cereblon identification is the chemical-mechanistic anchor of the molecular-glue branch, which otherwise would be left out of the citation.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the prize would bundle two lineages, PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) and molecular glues (Handa, Ito, Gray), under a three-person limit, so real contributors are omitted whichever trio is chosen. Clinical benefit of degraders is also not yet firmly established, and I cannot verify trial outcomes myself, so the committee could reasonably judge this a few years early. Nitrogenase, by contrast, has decades of independent confirmation but an unresolved catalytic mechanism.

responses.point: Daniel ranks B011 first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, treating the molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray) as a distinct lineage and a credit-allocation problem, and also sees ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B061) as a major chemistry achievement.
responses.response: I agree that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex design rules made PROTACs rational, and I take seriously that Handa's claim is a different lineage. But a PROTAC-only citation leaves out the thalidomide mechanism, which is the clearest case where the chemistry explained a drug. I would accept Ciulli in the third position if the majority prefers a PROTAC-centred citation, but then the prize should not be worded as covering glues. On B061, I agree the delivery chemistry is impressive, but the lipid inventions are spread across many academic and industrial groups, and I find the attribution less clean than for B011.

responses.point: Peter ranks long-range electron transfer through proteins (B058, Gray and Winkler) first, as a mature physical framework for respiratory and photosynthetic electron transfer, and ranks B011 only fourth because clinical validation is still emerging.
responses.response: I share the view that B058 is a rigorous, independently confirmed mechanistic framework with a clean two-person credit, and I find that persuasive. My disagreement is about maturity for B011: the ternary-complex chemistry and the proteasome-dependent mechanism have been reproduced widely, and the Nobel criterion is a discovery with demonstrated consequences for chemistry, not an approved drug. I would, however, concede that the clinical record is a real uncertainty. I would put B058 above most other candidates on this shortlist for mechanism, but its recognition is more of a retrospective prize, whereas B011 is changing what chemists do now.

responses.point: Johan ranks B011 first as a new pharmacological principle that removes rather than blocks a target and has consequences already, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, and thinks the timing is good but arguably slightly early.
responses.response: We agree on the principle and the timing. Where I qualify his view is on the glue branch: a trio of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli is the clean PROTAC story, but the thalidomide mechanism through cereblon is the better-measured chemistry, and I would not want to leave it out. I also note that Johan's second choice, sequencing by synthesis, is not on the shortlist, so I cannot support it here.

responses.point: Peter Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (B055, Hartwig and Buchwald) first on the basis of daily use in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis and a very clean two-person attribution, and ranks B011 only seventh.
responses.response: The adoption argument for B055 is strong and the credit is clean, and I do not dispute that. My reservation is that, after the 2010 coupling prize, C-N coupling is a major extension of an already recognised catalytic concept, whereas B011 creates a new capability, removing a protein by chemical design. I do not think low opening support for B011 from Peter means the science is weaker; it is a difference in how we weigh novelty against ubiquity, and I would like to hear whether the synthetic chemists see the degrader chemistry as chemically innovative.

uncertainties: Whether the prize should cover PROTACs only (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) or include the molecular-glue branch (Handa, with Ito and Gray omitted).
Whether clinical validation of degraders is sufficient yet, which I cannot verify myself.
Whether the nitrogenase mechanism (B008) is settled enough to rank above degraders, given that the E4 hydride and N2 binding remain debated.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile; none of the shortlisted candidates is in my own nucleotide-metabolism research area or my Umeå, Cold Spring Harbor or Wallenberg collaborations.
